standards.name: NIST CSF or ISO 27001 Controls Mapped to Systems
test: Export the NIST CSF/ISO 27001 control-to-system mapping matrix from the GRC workspace in ServiceNow ITSM.
Compare the matrix against the CMDB application list in ServiceNow ITSM for systems onboarded or retired in the past 12 months.
For five sampled systems open the linked evidence artifact in Confluence and match it to the stated implementation status.
Check the matrix record in ServiceNow ITSM for a last-reviewed date, owner sign-off and a documented update process.
Pass when every in-scope system is mapped with owner, status and evidence source, and all five sampled artifacts are current.

standards.name: No Direct Commits to Main or Master
test: Open Settings > Branches on every in-scope repository in GitHub Enterprise and review push restrictions on main/master.
Confirm the protection rule in GitHub Enterprise lists zero direct-push grantees, including admins and service accounts.
Push a test commit to main from a standard account and an admin account in a representative repo in GitHub Enterprise.
Export the prior 90 days of push events for main/master from the GitHub Enterprise audit log and look for non-PR commits.
Pass when both test pushes are rejected and the 90-day audit log shows zero direct commits to main or master.

standards.name: No PII in Logs
test: Run the automated PII detection scan over the prior 24 hours of production log streams and open the scan report in Splunk.
Open the logging configuration for three sampled services in GitHub Enterprise and check masking rules apply at emission.
Search Splunk with SSN, email and cardholder regex patterns across FNOL intake and policy administration service logs.
Export the past 12 months of PII-in-logs findings from ServiceNow ITSM and check each was handled as a security incident.
Pass when both scans return zero unmasked PII, masking is configured in all three services and prior findings closed in SLA.

standards.name: No PR Open Beyond 48 Hours Without Action
test: Export all PRs opened in the past 60 days from GitHub Enterprise with opened and first-activity timestamps.
Flag every exported PR exceeding 48 hours with no approval, change request or hold note recorded in GitHub Enterprise.
For each flagged PR open the escalation notification record in Jira and confirm it was raised within the 48-hour window.
Open the stale-PR report on the engineering dashboard and confirm the alert rule exists and fired for each flagged PR.
Pass when every PR breaching 48 hours has a matching escalation record and the stale-PR alert fired for each instance.

standards.name: No Untested Public Methods
test: Run the public-method coverage report in SonarQube and list any public method with zero covering test invocations.
For ten sampled public methods across services open their unit tests in GitHub Enterprise and check a success-path assertion.
For the same ten methods confirm at least one principal error-case test exists in GitHub Enterprise.
Open the Definition of Done page in Confluence and check it requires unit tests for new or modified public methods.
Open the CI workflow in GitHub Actions and identify the step or coverage gate that blocks untested public methods.
Pass when the report shows zero untested public methods and all ten sampled methods cover success plus one error case.

standards.name: Non-Functional Requirements
test: Open the project's design-approval package in Confluence and locate the version-controlled NFR document.
Check in Confluence that all five NFR dimensions carry quantified targets, not placeholders.
Open the approval record in Jira and confirm both required sign-offs are timestamped before the design-approval milestone.
Trace two randomly sampled NFRs to a design decision or acceptance-test criterion recorded in Jira.
For systems in production open the monitoring dashboard and check each quantified NFR has a live metric or scheduled audit.
Pass when all five dimensions show quantified dual-approved targets and both sampled NFRs trace to downstream artifacts.

standards.name: On-Call Rotation
test: Open the on-call schedules in PagerDuty and check primary and secondary coverage for the current and next two periods.
Open the on-call rotation policy page in Confluence and check handoff steps, escalation tiers and max consecutive hours.
For three engineers on active rotations open the training system record and confirm a completed shadow shift per service.
Open the escalation policy configuration in PagerDuty for two sampled production services and check auto-escalation timings.
Pass when every production service shows gap-free primary and secondary coverage and all three sampled shadow shifts exist.

standards.name: Onboarding Guide for New Developers
test: Open the team onboarding guide in Confluence and check domain context, system landscape, access requests and local setup.
Open the guide's change history in GitHub Enterprise and find the most recent joiner's corrective update commit.
Follow the local-setup section on a clean VM and note any undocumented manual steps needed to reach a working environment.
Pass when all four sections are present and non-stub, the joiner's fix commit exists and setup needs no out-of-band steps.

standards.name: OpenAPI 3.0 Specs Required
test: Pull the OpenAPI 3.0 spec for one randomly selected API from its repository in GitHub Enterprise.
Run the Spectral lint stage on the spec in the CI pipeline (GitHub Actions) and open the rule-violation report.
Open the route list for the API in the API gateway console and compare deployed paths against the spec's path list.
Open the architecture review sign-off log in Confluence and check the spec was approved before the last release gate.
Pass when the lint shows zero critical errors, no undocumented routes are deployed and the sign-off references the spec.

standards.name: OpenAPI Spec Auto-Generated
test: Open the CI workflow for each HTTP API repo in GitHub Actions and locate the non-skippable spec-generation step.
Push a branch with a malformed annotation in GitHub Enterprise and trigger the build in GitHub Actions.
Confirm in GitHub Actions that the broken build failed and produced no deployable artifact.
Compare the spec published in the API gateway against the artifact of the latest successful GitHub Actions build.
Check a downstream consumer repo in GitHub Enterprise for an import or generated client referencing the published spec.
Pass when the broken build is blocked, the published spec matches the build artifact and a downstream dependency exists.

standards.name: Ownership, Classification, and Refresh Frequency Documented
test: Export the full asset list from the data catalog with owner, sensitivity classification and refresh-frequency columns.
Check the export shows all three attributes populated for 100% of assets using labels from the enterprise scheme.
For 10 sampled Confidential-PII or Restricted assets open access controls in the data platform and compare to classification.
Open the most recent periodic catalog review report in Confluence and check it is dated within the last 90 days.
Trace each gap listed in the review to a remediation ticket in Jira and record its open or closed status.
Pass when 100% of assets carry all three attributes, no sampled access exceeds classification and every gap has a ticket.

standards.name: PRs Reviewed Within Four Hours
test: Export PR event logs for the past 30 days from GitHub Enterprise with submission and first-review timestamps.
Compute first-review latency in business hours for each exported PR and flag any exceeding four business hours.
Open the review coverage schedule in Confluence and check review duty is assigned across all squad time zones.
Open the team working agreement in Confluence and confirm it cites the four-business-hour first-review commitment.
Pass when the 30-day export shows first substantive reviews within four business hours and coverage closes timezone gaps.

standards.name: Pairing Required for Complex Features
test: Open sprint planning notes for the last two sprints in Confluence and list features designated complex requiring pairing.
For each designated feature open the work item in Jira and confirm two named engineers are assigned.
Open the commit history for each feature in GitHub Enterprise and check both authors committed across the full build period.
Open each feature's PR in GitHub Enterprise and check any solo-author submission carries an approved pairing exception.
Pass when every designated complex feature shows dual-author involvement end to end or a recorded approved exception.

standards.name: Performance Baseline Established
test: Open each in-scope service's performance baseline record in Confluence and check p50/p95/p99, throughput and CPU/memory.
Check the baseline timestamp in Confluence postdates the service's most recent significant release.
Open the latest post-release performance test report in the CI pipeline (GitHub Actions) and find the baseline comparison.
Open the release runbook in Confluence and locate the mandatory baseline-comparison step before production promotion.
Pass when every baseline covers all metrics at reference load, is current and the latest report compares deltas against it.

standards.name: Performance Metrics Tracked
test: Open the model inventory and check each production model lists its metrics, computation cadence and validation benchmarks.
For five sampled models pull the last three cadence-period performance records from the model inventory.
Check each sampled record was computed on schedule and logged in the model inventory, not held in ad hoc analyst files.
Open the dashboard access log and confirm documented visibility for the model owner and the model risk function.
Pass when all five sampled models show on-schedule logged metrics against benchmarks with owner and risk-function access.

standards.name: Performance Under 5 Second Load
test: Run the documented concurrent-user load against the production dashboard in the load-testing tool and record render time.
Review aggregation table definitions, query execution plans and cache configuration in the BI platform's admin console.
Pull the UAT performance test log and any post-data-model-change re-test records from Confluence and check sign-off.
Pass when measured and logged initial render times are 5 seconds or less under typical load with tuning artifacts in place.

standards.name: PlantUML or Mermaid
test: List every architecture and design diagram in active project documentation in Confluence and note each source format.
Search each repo in GitHub Enterprise for a committed .puml or .mmd/Mermaid source file matching every listed diagram.
Open the documentation site build in GitHub Actions and confirm diagrams render from source at build time, not uploads.
Open a test PR changing one line of a diagram source in GitHub Enterprise and check a text diff and rendered preview show.
Pass when zero diagrams exist only as binary drawing-tool exports and the test PR shows a readable diff with auto-render.

standards.name: Prioritization Criteria
test: Open the published Prioritization Criteria document in Confluence and check weights, scoring scale and board approval date.
Check the document history in Confluence for any criterion or weight change lacking a formal board resolution.
For five requests approved in the past two quarters open the scoring worksheets in the PPM tool (Clarity/Planview).
Compare each worksheet's criteria and weights to the published document and check composite scores predate backlog entry.
Search the PPM tool for any worksheet using a criterion or weight absent from the approved document.
Pass when all five worksheets match the published criteria and weights exactly and no per-request adjustments are found.
